findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify an availability/health alarm for the new rebar-mcp service (e.g. a CloudWatch alarm on /health or the container state wired to the existing rebar-gerrit-alerts SNS topic, mirroring monitoring_autodeploy.tf), not just the retire-cap alert.
evidence: esok scope: container 'healthcheck hitting the MCP /health endpoint' and '/health ... feeds foxterrier's retire check; it does not gate the deploy'
foxterrier: 'over a hard cap, emit an SNS alert (the terraform rebar-gerrit-alerts topic)' — this alert is scoped to retention-cap, not to service-down/unhealthy
monitoring.tf already defines the rebar-gerrit-alerts SNS topic and the repo has a monitoring_autodeploy.tf pattern, so an mcp-health alarm is idiomatic here but not called out
findings.finding: The epic stands up a new durable network-reachable service (rebar-mcp) but does not specify a CloudWatch alarm on the service's own health/availability; the only alert called out is on the blue-green retire-cap edge case (SNS to rebar-gerrit-alerts), plus a compose container healthcheck. A silent mcp outage (container down after restart backoff exhaustion, or unhealthy but not over the retire cap) would not page an operator.
findings.location: esok (cibophobic-holohedral-esok) /health gauge + foxterrier retire-cap SNS alert; AC line 'the mcp HTTP service + nginx /mcp/ switchable upstream + /health gauge land'
scenarios: The mcp container crash-loops and exits restart backoff; clients get 502 through the /mcp/ edge but no alarm fires because in_flight/retire-cap logic never triggers
The service boots but /health degrades post-cutover; the deploy already succeeded (deploy does not gate on health beyond the new-container check) and no ongoing availability alarm exists

evidence: Plan: 'Copilot (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` `headers`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml` `bearer_token_env_var` / `http_headers`) static-bearer-over-HTTP are verified against those tools' current official docs (research 2026-08-24; citations recorded in the ADR)'
docs/mcp-auth.md §4 lists ONLY Claude paths: 'Claude Code `--header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` / Claude.ai `static_headers`' — Copilot/Codex are not covered by rebar's own docs
The repo's Codex knowledge (docs/session-id-shims.md) covers `~/.codex/config.toml` `shell_environment_policy` only, not MCP-server auth keys `bearer_token_env_var`/`http_headers`
resolve_symbol cannot probe these (external non-Python tool config keys); citations live in the not-yet-landed ADR — EVIDENCE CLASS: Unverified (Claude = Verified; Copilot/Codex = Unverified)
findings.finding: The plan asserts the Copilot (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` `headers`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml` `bearer_token_env_var` / `http_headers`) static-bearer config keys are 'verified against those tools' current official docs', but the supporting citations are deferred into the ADR (deft-evolutive-mosasaur, child #1) which is not yet landed — so the exact config-file keys the client connection depends on are unverifiable in the plan itself, and only Claude's path is confirmed in-repo (docs/mcp-auth.md §4 names only Claude Code `--header` / Claude.ai `static_headers`, NOT Copilot or Codex).
scenarios: A client's actual MCP-server auth key differs from the plan's asserted key (e.g. a nested `requestInit.headers.Authorization` vs a top-level `headers`), so the client silently fails to send the bearer and the connection 401s
The key was correct at 2026-08-24 research time but the client shipped a schema change before olm lands

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the blue-green rollback path explicitly: on a bad cutover, atomically flip the nginx upstream back to the retained prior release, and add it as a foxterrier acceptance check.
evidence: Plan states 'immutable release + atomic nginx-upstream flip + retire-when-idle with retention/cap/alert' but the rollback described is for the enforcement flip ('reversible by unset'), not for a bad cutover.
Retention implies the prior release survives, but the explicit flip-back-on-bad-release rollback is not stated as an AC.
findings.finding: The blue-green autodeploy specifies build→cutover→retire with retention/cap, but does not explicitly state the rollback path when a NEW mcp release is bad post-cutover (i.e. flip the nginx upstream back to the still-retained prior release).
findings.location: Decomposition child 3 (panicky-sylphish-foxterrier) / AC line 'The autodeploy blue-green mcp target lands'
scenarios: A new mcp release passes /health but exhibits a runtime defect after cutover; operator needs to revert quickly to the retained prior release.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a lightweight capability-probe SPIKE (or fold one into the ADR/olm-precursor) that connects each of copilot/codex/claude to a throwaway static-bearer HTTP MCP endpoint and records the exact working config keys, gating the infra slices on that probe so a client capability gap is caught before the full build commits.
evidence: Dependency order: infra (esok), secrets (avians), autodeploy (foxterrier) all depend only on the ADR (mosasaur); the first actual client-connection check is olm (dep: esok, avians) and the live proof is jackal (dep: olm)
Plan: 'exact config-file keys pinned from OBSERVED current client docs' is scheduled inside olm, i.e. AFTER the infra it connects to is built
T3 checklist: 'A critical capability gap routes to a SPIKE before committing the full plan' — no such probe precedes the infra slices
findings.finding: The plan commits the full infra build (esok compose/nginx, avians secrets, foxterrier blue-green) before any of the three external clients' static-bearer-over-HTTP capability against a custom self-hosted MCP endpoint has been proven, and routes no capability-probe SPIKE ahead of those slices — a client capability gap would surface only at olm/jackal.
scenarios: A client turns out not to support static bearer against an arbitrary self-hosted HTTP MCP server (only OAuth/DCR), invalidating the 'none of the three requires OAuth' premise after infra has shipped
One client rejects a non-public / self-signed-adjacent custom endpoint, requiring an exposure/auth redesign post-build

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the starling AGENTS.md 'MCP-required policy' specify the fallback for a failed/unavailable MCP sub-step (transient cutover/retire windows, auth failure) — e.g. bounded retry across the atomic flip, and whether/when a local-CLI fallback is permitted vs. hard-fail — so agents have defined behavior when an MCP call does not succeed.
evidence: Plan: 'so the copilot, codex, and claude clients drive ALL rebar operations through it (dogfooding)'
Plan item 7: 'guidance/docs: AGENTS.md MCP-required policy'

ABSENCE: neither the epic body nor the starling/olm slice states what an agent should do when an MCP call fails or the endpoint is briefly unreachable — yet the design itself introduces transient-unavailability windows (blue-green 'atomic nginx-upstream flip', 'retire-when-idle', SIGTERM grace) and a fail-closed auth edge (per-client bearer PATs).
findings.finding: The starling slice introduces an AGENTS.md 'MCP-required policy' ('the copilot, codex, and claude clients drive ALL rebar operations through it') — an LLM-agent decision rule — but specifies no fallback behavior for a failed/unavailable MCP sub-step (e.g. during the blue-green cutover window, retire-when-idle, or an auth/endpoint failure).
findings.location: Decomposition item 7 (starling) / AGENTS.md MCP-required policy; Summary paragraph 1 ('drive ALL rebar operations through it')
scenarios: An agent mid-task issues a rebar op through MCP during the atomic upstream flip and the request fails; with an unqualified 'MCP-required' policy the agent has no defined recovery (retry? fall back to local CLI? abort?).
A per-client bearer PAT is rotated/misconfigured and the MCP edge returns 401/403; the agent has no specified behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the epic's post-flip-closing children (starling, jackal, and goose itself) obtain a valid completion-verifier cert under the enforced env, or confirm their close-anchors fall on/before goose's grandfather boundary so they stay advisory.
evidence: Child b173 AC2: 'a ticket closed AFTER the boundary without a valid completion-verifier cert FAILs rebar verify-opcert (exit 1, enforced)'.
Parent decomposition orders goose (5) before starling (7) and jackal (8), and parent AC7 requires 'Every child ticket is closed.'
b173 sets opcert_enforce_since to 'the current merged-log tip' at its land — sibling tickets that close after that anchor are descendants of the boundary and therefore enforced.
No sibling roster block states how starling/jackal (docs + operator-performed slices) obtain a completion-verifier cert once the gate is enforcing.
findings.finding: The enforcement flip in child goose (verify.require_environment + opcert_enforce_since set together, boundary at a deploy-time anchor) creates a forward-facing consumer impact on the epic's OWN later-closing sibling tickets: any child whose close-anchor is a descendant of goose's boundary must present an MCP-minted completion-verifier cert to pass verify-opcert, yet no child names how the epic's remaining slices (e.g. starling, jackal) obtain that cert post-flip.
scenarios: goose lands and flips the gate; starling then closes without an MCP-minted completion-verifier cert and its close FAILs verify-opcert at the merge-gate, blocking parent AC7 (all children closed).
jackal (operator-performed, no code) closes after the boundary and is likewise enforced.
findings.suggested_fix: State in goose (and/or the parent) that the deploy-time grandfather boundary is anchored such that the epic's own remaining children close as pre-boundary/advisory, OR that their completion closes route through the MCP-minted completion-verifier cert path once the service is live.
